## Why visit

A particularly useful Chorlton stop because it combines regional cask, a meaningful cider offering and an independent kitchen. Its roots as The Bar make it part of the neighbourhood’s established beer culture rather than a recent generic taproom. The cider cool box is worth explicitly asking about; the selection can include perry as well as cider. Build it into a compact circuit with Beer House and Fell, and consider making it the food stop if the kitchen’s actual operating days fit your visit.

## Beer

Changing cask from local and wider independent breweries, with keg and bottles alongside. CAMRA identifies Marble, Pictish and Pomona Island among its changing cask brewers.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly says some bag-in-box products meet its real-cider guidelines and occasionally perry is stocked. Ask which products qualify; the whole selection is not automatically real cider. CAMRA also names Celtic Marches and Seacider among boxed cider leads; qualification must be checked for the particular product, not inferred from the maker alone.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Nora’s Kitchen is reported to provide pizza on selected days and Sunday roasts. Confirm the current operator, service days and any tasting-menu event directly.

## Plan the visit

Card/digital payment only in the current listing. Do not treat a recurring tasting-menu pattern as confirmation of a November event.

**Getting there:** Walk from Chorlton tram stop; convenient for Fell Chorlton and Beer House.
